subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve parallel distinct ACP child sessions and require a narrow launch-readiness fix, or intentionally serialize/throttle rapid ACPX child launches?
rationale: Current source and tests preserve different ACP session keys running in parallel, so changing that behavior to avoid this failure is a compatibility and product decision rather than a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Preserve Parallelism
options.body: Run a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude reproduction and fix the launch-readiness boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

options.title: Gate Rapid ACPX Launches
options.body: Intentionally serialize or throttle rapid ACPX child launches and update tests/docs to make the reduced concurrency contract explicit.

options.title: Hold For Fresh Evidence
options.body: Keep the issue in needs-info until a current live repro identifies whether the old first-child no-output symptom still occurs.

recommendation.title: Preserve Parallelism
recommendation.body: Run a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude reproduction and fix the launch-readiness boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has recent adjacent ACPX runtime and current-main ownership signals, making it the best available owner for the launch-readiness versus concurrency tradeoff.
